title: Mississippi's 4th Congressional District election, 2026
description: Mississippi's 4th Congressional District covers the southeastern region of the state, including the Gulf Coast communities of Gulfport, Biloxi, and Pascagoula, as well as Hattiesburg and inland areas. Incumbent Republican Mike Ezell, a former Jackson County Sheriff first elected in 2022 after defeating then-incumbent Steven Palazzo in the primary, is seeking a third term. He faces Democratic nominee Jeffrey Hulum III, a U.S. Army veteran and state representative from Gulfport, and Independent candidate Carl Boyanton, a small business owner and nonprofit founder. The district is considered safely Republican by nonpartisan election forecasters, with the Cook Political Report, Inside Elections, and Sabato's Crystal Ball all rating it as Solid/Safe Republican.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for this race as of the research date. The district is rated Solid/Safe Republican by major nonpartisan forecasters.

candidates.name: Mike Ezell
candidates.summary: Mike Ezell is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Mississippi's 4th Congressional District, first elected in 2022. He spent over 42 years in law enforcement, most recently as Jackson County Sheriff, and serves on the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee as Chairman of the Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation Subcommittee, as well as the House Natural Resources Committee.

candidates.name: Jeffrey Hulum III
candidates.summary: Jeffrey Hulum III is a Democratic member of the Mississippi House of Representatives representing District 119 (Gulfport area) since 2022 and the Democratic nominee for Mississippi's 4th Congressional District. A 22-year U.S. Army veteran who retired as a Sergeant Major with six combat tours, he founded the nonprofit Extend A Hand, Help A Friend to fight food insecurity on the Gulf Coast. In the state legislature, he serves as Vice-Chair for Marine Resources and sits on the Gaming, Military Affairs, Ports/Harbors/Airports, and Tourism committees.

candidates.name: Carl Boyanton
candidates.summary: Carl Boyanton is an Independent candidate running for Mississippi's 4th Congressional District. He is a small business owner and founder of Farmer Fresh Produce, which grew to employ around 100 workers, and co-founded the nonprofit Farmed Fresh for Mississippi to deliver fresh food to veterans and families in need. Boyanton describes himself as a principled conservative alternative and previously ran for this seat as a Republican in 2022 and 2024.

forecast.rationale: No public polling exists for this race, which limits certainty. However, the available structural indicators are unambiguous: major nonpartisan forecasters (Cook Political Report, Inside Elections, Sabato's Crystal Ball) all rate Mississippi's 4th Congressional District as Solid/Safe Republican. Incumbent Mike Ezell, a former Jackson County Sheriff first elected in 2022, is seeking a third term. Democrat Jeffrey Hulum III is a credible challenger—a state representative, 22-year U.S. Army veteran—but faces an uphill climb in a district with a strong Republican lean. Independent Carl Boyanton, previously a Republican primary candidate in 2022 and 2024, offers a conservative-splinter option but does not appear positioned to mount a serious challenge. Without polls to test these assumptions, medium confidence is appropriate, but the district's fundamentals strongly support a Republican hold with a large margin.
